items.description: App rendered in MemoryRouter at /stock/file mounts the file-stock form page without crashing
The SKU input on the file-stock form carries its design-guide data-testid attribute
The location input on the file-stock form carries its design-guide data-testid attribute
The quantity input on the file-stock form carries its design-guide data-testid attribute
The inventory_code input on the file-stock form carries its design-guide data-testid attribute
The submit control on the file-stock form carries its design-guide data-testid attribute
POSTing a stock record to the API with a uuid-suffixed SKU, location, quantity, and inventory_code returns a 2xx response indicating the record was durably saved
The boundary layer (app/routes/) contains no import of the SQLAlchemy Session object, satisfying the layering contract that the session must not cross into the boundary

Database write operations (session.add, session.commit, or equivalent) appear only in app/repositories/ and in no service or boundary module, satisfying the persistence-only-in-repository half of the layering contract

The service layer (app/services/) contains no SQLAlchemy ORM imports—neither Session nor any mapped model class—satisfying the ORM-only contract for the service tier (distinct from the routes-vs-session layering check)
The boundary layer (app/routes/) contains no SQLAlchemy ORM model class imports, satisfying the ORM-only contract for the boundary tier (distinct from the routes-vs-session layering check)
No hardcoded database connection string exists anywhere in the application source; the DATABASE_URL is read exclusively from the process environment (twelve-factor config-from-env)
Integration tests connect via DATABASE_URL to a real Lakebase branch database and do not use an in-memory SQLite or any mocked DB driver; the driver module in use is the Databricks Postgres driver
An attempt to persist a stock record with a NULL value in any of the quantity, sku, location, or inventory_code columns against the real branch database is rejected by the NOT NULL constraint

A direct insert of a row with quantity = -1 into stock_records on the real branch database is rejected by the ck_stock_records_quantity_non_negative CHECK constraint; no row with a negative quantity is stored
The service layer raises a rejection error when a write is attempted with a negative quantity value, before the call reaches the repository or the database CHECK constraint
A boundary validation error response for an invalid stock filing request includes the specific offending field name in the error payload rather than a generic message

The Alembic migration for stock_records can be downgraded one step and then upgraded again on the real branch in a single operation without error (marked @pytest.mark.migration; never downgraded past base)
Rows seeded with a per-run-unique key before the migration is applied are present in stock_records with their original field values intact after the upgrade completes on the real branch
App rendered in MemoryRouter at the stock-detail route mounts the stock-detail page without crashing
The quantity display element on the stock-detail page carries its design-guide data-testid attribute
The inventory_code display element on the stock-detail page carries its design-guide data-testid attribute
GETting a previously POSTed stock record via the API returns the exact quantity that was filed
GETting a previously POSTed stock record via the API returns the exact combined inventory_code that was filed
The boundary layer (app/routes/) returns JSON responses and contains no server-side template rendering call, consistent with renders_via: react declared in the architecture
After the file-stock form is submitted for a SKU and location that already has a record, no error element is visible in the UI
After POSTing stock twice for the same uuid-suffixed SKU and location pair, the API returns exactly one record for that pair
After POSTing stock twice for the same uuid-suffixed SKU and location pair, the second POST response is a 2xx with no error surfaced
Filing two stock records with an identical (sku, location) pair against the real branch database results in exactly one row stored, enforced by the composite unique constraint on stock_records

A concurrent upsert for the same (sku, location) pair on the real branch executes inside a single transaction, resulting in exactly one row with no duplicate, verified by a per-run-unique seed key and row count assertion
When a collision triggers an in-place upsert on an existing (sku, location) row, the created_at timestamp on that row is unchanged after the write
